rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~93–94% 25bp / ~6% 50bp (CME FedWatch via Reuters); ECB Dec ~88–92%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~70–75%; BoC Dec ~44% (from ~60% pre-CPI)
rows.read: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave no hint on rates, so his colleagues' calls for a December hike still set the tone and bets stayed near certain. Canada's calm inflation figures cut the odds of a Bank of Canada hike to below even. Europe, Britain and Japan are still expected to hike, but US rates are rising faster, which keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Empire State Nov 7.8 (fcst 16.7; Oct 25.5); euro-area IP Sep +0.2% m/m (fcst +0.3%), −1.5% y/y; Japan Q3 GDP −0.1% annualized; China Oct retail sales +0.4% y/y (fcst +0.8%)
rows.read: A New York factory survey cooled sharply, though hiring in it was the strongest in four years, so it did little to the US picture. Euro-area factories barely grew, and Japan and China also came in soft. The US still looks firmer than most, and US retail sales on Tuesday are the next check.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Canada CPI Oct 3.1% y/y (fcst 3.2%), core median 2.0%, trim 1.8%; UK CPI Oct fcst 3.6% (Sep 3.5%), Wed 1:00 AM CT; Brent −3.6%
rows.read: Canadian inflation held steady, with core prices near the Bank of Canada's goal, so energy costs are not yet spreading into everyday prices there. US inflation is still well above the Fed's goal, which keeps the pressure to hike. Falling oil should ease price worries a little, and UK inflation on Wednesday matters most for the pound.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Nasdaq −1.3%, S&P 500 −1.0% midday; AUD/USD ~0.675 (lowest since January); USD/JPY ~159.6; USD/CHF ~0.840
rows.read: US tech stocks fell sharply ahead of Nvidia's results, souring the mood. The Aussie and kiwi, which track market mood, slipped toward their lows. Yet the safe-haven franc and yen got little lift, because rising US rates still matter more to them than the scare.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent settled $92.44 (−3.6%), WTI $85.72 (−3.2%); IEA Q4 surplus ~1.7 mb/d; gold ~$3,867, low ~$3,840 (13-month low)
rows.read: Oil fell hard as traders bet that supply will outrun demand, with Gulf flows nearly back to normal. That helps energy buyers such as Japan and the euro area and takes support away from the Canadian dollar. Gold's slide to a 13-month low adds to the Aussie's troubles.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Nov 3: hedge funds for USD, JPY, AUD, GBP; against NZD, CAD, EUR; Nov 10 report delayed by Veterans Day
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro, and the dollar's run keeps paying them. Their large bet on the yen keeps losing money as it weakens. Big bets against the euro, Aussie and kiwi could unwind fast on good news.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.13%
rows.read: Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs above 5%. Higher yields support the dollar for now, but a growing deficit is a worry if buyers start asking for more. France's debt troubles keep weighing on the euro.
